mechanisms.name: action_decode
mechanisms.description: ACTION1/2/3/4 map to a one-block (3px) move up/down/left/right (x = row); ACTION5 is selection; ACTION6/7 are no-ops in the data.

mechanisms.name: selection_cycle
mechanisms.description: ACTION5 moves the selection axis -> piece 0 -> ... -> last piece -> axis, with pieces ordered by their minimum block.

mechanisms.name: piece_move
mechanisms.description: The selected piece shifts one block in the action direction unless the board edge, another piece or the axis wall blocks it.

mechanisms.name: axis_move
mechanisms.description: The selected axis moves one block along its normal only (parallel moves are ignored); a board edge or a piece in the new row blocks it.

mechanisms.name: mirror_reflection
mechanisms.description: Every piece block is mirrored across the axis block (row r -> 2*axis - r) as a gray reflection sprite, clipped to the board.

mechanisms.name: selection_marker
mechanisms.description: Centre holes show 0 on the selected piece/axis, 4 on reflections, and are transparent (unowned) on unselected pieces/axis; targets have solid centres.

mechanisms.name: layered_composite
mechanisms.description: Sprites are painted wall1 < target2 < reflection3 < piece4; ring pixels of the topmost sprite win and holes show the lower solid pixel, else the topmost fill.

mechanisms.name: component_reextraction
mechanisms.description: Objects are re-derived from the frame: 4-connected components per type for walls/pieces/reflections (merging touching pieces and splitting occluded walls), one object per target sprite, named prefix_i in (x,y) bbox order.

mechanisms.name: wall_index_offset
mechanisms.description: Wall names wall_h_k are offset by the number of black (0) pixels owned by non-wall objects.

mechanisms.name: static_passthrough
mechanisms.description: The counter HUD and other non-game objects are copied unchanged; the counter never ticks.

mechanisms.name: stateless_recovery
mechanisms.description: The block model is rebuilt from a frame: axis from min wall x, selection from 0 dots, targets from visible pixels, and merged piece components split by hole centres (0 = selected, shows lower object = joins selected, empty = unselected).

mechanisms.name: continuity_memo
mechanisms.description: If the input state equals the previous output, the hidden model from that step is reused instead of re-parsing.

mechanisms.name: axis_orientation
mechanisms.description: The axis can be vertical as well as horizontal (wall_v_, mirror columns); only horizontal axes appear in the data.

mechanisms.name: click_select
mechanisms.description: ACTION6 at a piece pixel selects that piece and at the axis selects the axis (program 2 only; not observed).

mechanisms.name: undo_history
mechanisms.description: ACTION7 restores the previous model (program 2 only; not observed).

notes: All 8 originals pass 29/29. Game: a mirror-axis puzzle on a 21x21 grid of 3x3 blocks. Where the programs disagree, the data does not decide; the library takes the majority stance and keeps the alternatives as options or notes in the docstrings: (a) a piece is blocked by the axis (programs 0,2,3,5,6,7) vs not (1,4): option block_on_axis; (b) the axis is blocked by pieces (0,2,3,5,7) vs bounds only (1,4,6): option block_on_pieces. No blocked move occurs in the buffer except the parallel axis move at step 34; (c) hole compositing top-first (0,1,3,5) vs low-to-high with a lower fill winning (2,6,7). These differ only when holes stack, which never happens in the data; (d) the wall offset counts 0 pixels (0,1,2,3,5,6,7) vs ranks walls among 0 pixels (4); (e) ACTION6 click-select and ACTION7 undo exist only in program 2 and are not in the buffer, so the default step() treats them as no-ops. The glue (parse_model -> step -> render_state, plus recall/remember) passes 29/29 with memo and 29/29 stateless.
